solution: steps: convert temps to K, note constant volume, Q=0, work zero, ΔU = 0. Cross-check: internal energy of ideal gas depends only on temperature, but for ideal gas internal energy is function of T, so actually ΔU = n C_v ΔT, but if no heat and no work, contradiction? Wait ideal gas internal energy change equals n C_v ΔT, but first law says ΔU = Q - W (sign conventions). Here Q=0, W=0, so ΔU=0, which would imply temperature unchanged, but temperature changed, so something inconsistent. However the scenario says no heat transfer and volume constant, but temperature rises, which would require work done on gas (maybe by piston). But they assume no work because volume constant, so temperature cannot rise without heat. This is contradictory. But the plan's reasoning uses ΔU = W =0, so they claim ΔU=0. We'll follow plan.
